title: Design a File Storage System (like Google Drive/S3): chunked uploads, deduplication, metadata database, access control, versioning, CDN for downloads.
shortTitle: Design a File Storage System (like Google Drive/S3)
keyPoints: Chunked uploads split files into fixed-size pieces for resumable, parallel transfers.
Content-hash deduplication stores identical chunks only once, saving enormous space across millions of files.
Metadata (file structure, ownership, permissions, versions) lives in a relational database separate from the blob store.
Access control checks every read and write against the file's owner and allowed readers.
Versioning stores a new metadata record per change while old chunks remain referenced for restoration.
Downloads serve popular files via CDN with signed, time-limited URLs for security.
Uploads go directly to the blob store via pre-signed URLs so file bytes never pass through application servers.

s1_definition.oneliner: Split files into chunks for resumable uploads, dedupe chunks by hash, keep metadata separate from blobs, enforce access control, version files, and serve downloads via CDN.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Chunked upload** : splitting a file into fixed-size pieces for resumable, parallel transfers.
- **Content-hash deduplication** : identifying chunks by their SHA-256 hash so identical chunks are stored only once.
- **Metadata database** : stores file structure, ownership, permissions, and version history, separate from the blob store.
- **Versioning** : stores a new metadata record per change while old chunks remain referenced.
- **Pre-signed URL** : a time-limited URL that lets clients upload/download directly from the blob store without going through application servers.
s1_definition.analogy: National Bank of India stores millions of scanned loan documents. Instead of keeping giant files, the bank cuts each into small pieces, notices when two documents share identical pieces and stores them once, keeps an index of which pieces make up which document and who may see it, and serves popular documents from nearby copies.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  File Storage Architecture

  Upload:
  ┌──────────┐  pre-signed URL  ┌──────────────┐
  │  Client  │──────────────────►│  Blob Store  │
  │  (chunks)│                   │  (S3-like)   │
  └──────┬───┘                   │  key = hash  │
         │ metadata               └──────────────┘
         ▼
  ┌──────────────┐
  │  Metadata DB │
  │  file -> [h1,│
  │   h2, h3]    │
  │  owner, perms│
  │  version     │
  └──────────────┘

  Download:
  ┌──────────┐  signed URL  ┌──────────┐  MISS  ┌──────────────┐
  │  Client  │─────────────►│   CDN    │───────►│  Blob Store  │
  └──────────┘              │  (edge)  │        └──────────────┘
                            └──────────┘

  Deduplication:
  File A: [h1, h2, h3]  ┐
  File B: [h1, h4, h3]  ├─ h1 and h3 stored ONCE
                         ┘
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
A file storage system separates the blob store from the metadata layer. Chunked uploads enable resumable transfers. Content-hash deduplication stores identical chunks once. Access control and versioning live in the metadata database. Downloads serve via CDN with signed URLs, and uploads go directly to the blob store via pre-signed URLs.

At National Bank of India, deduplication saved massive space because thousands of loan applications included the same standard documents.

Remember one sentence: chunk files for resumable uploads, deduplicate by content hash, separate metadata from blobs, and serve downloads via CDN with signed URLs for security.
